name: Autosomal Dominant Spastic Paraplegia Type 42

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Autosomal Dominant Spastic Paraplegia

criteria.description: Progressive lower limb spasticity and weakness
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variant in the ATP13A2 gene
Exclusion of other causes of spastic paraplegia by clinical and laboratory evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive lower limb spasticity and weakness with a positive family history and identification of a pathogenic ATP13A2 variant
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Degeneration of the lateral corticospinal tracts

common.symptomName: Impaired vibration sensation in the lower limbs

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic and inflammatory causes
imaging: MRI brain and spinal cord may show mild corticospinal tract atrophy
other: Electromyography may show mild distal neuropathy
Nerve conduction studies typically normal or mildly abnormal

distinguishingFeatures: SPG7 caused by mutations in SPG7 gene
Upper and lower motor neuron signs
No family history in most cases

redFlags: Rapid progression over weeks to months
Presence of lower motor neuron signs
Signs of systemic illness or metabolic disorder
references: Orphanet: Autosomal Dominant Spastic Paraplegia Type 42, ORPHA:171863
Harding AE. Hereditary spastic paraplegias. Semin Neurol. 1993;13(4):333-342.
Fink JK. Hereditary spastic paraplegia: clinical principles and genetic advances. Semin Neurol. 2014;34(3):293-305.
